name: TellTide
subcategory: feedback widget, private inbox, and public roadmap
tagline: Embed a widget, triage reviews and bugs in a private inbox, publish a public roadmap

pricing.notes: Homepage and FAQ on 2026-08-22 list Pro at $34/month or $348/year ($29/month). No per-user pricing.
pricing.freeTier: There is no usable free plan. A 7-day Pro trial requires a card; unpaid accounts cannot create apps or collect feedback.

tiers.name: Unpaid
tiers.limits: Account shell only. Cannot create apps or collect feedback.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited apps and feedback, widget, inbox, public roadmap, API credentials, custom branding, Excel export, advanced analytics.
tiers.notes: Yearly is $348. 7-day trial requires a card.

pricing.billingTerms: Monthly ($34) or yearly ($348, shown as $29/month). 7-day Pro trial with a card on file. Cancel before the trial ends and you are not charged. No per-user pricing.

verdictSummary: The product is a widget, a private inbox, and an optional public roadmap. A competent agent can one-shot that on Next.js and SQLite in a sitting. What you buy is a hosted embed that works on a real domain, credentials, and not running the box. There is no network or data moat: your users already belong to you.
coreLoopDIY: Embed a typed feedback widget, store submissions in a private inbox with statuses, and publish selected feature requests to a public roadmap with votes and comments.
requirements: a public HTTPS host if you want the widget on a real site
whatYouLose: hosted widget CDN and domain origin checks
multi-app API credentials you did not have to mint
a public roadmap you did not have to deploy
inbox already wired to an HTTP API
moatNotes: No structural moat. The product is the hosted loop.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay to paste one script, keep raw submissions private, and publish a roadmap without standing up auth, storage, or HTTPS. The DIY version is the same loop. The rent is uptime and not touching Docker.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Battle-tested Go feedback board. Read it if you want a real schema.

alternatives.name: Fider
alternatives.desc: The obvious voting board. Hosted free with a 250-item fair-use cap, or Docker if you want the lot.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and an email sender
facts.dataFormat: Posts, votes, comments, users, and tenants live in PostgreSQL.
facts.gapVsPaid: Fider is a public voting board, not a private inbox with typed reviews, bugs, and feature requests plus a branded embed widget.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted signup is clean. Self-host needs Docker, Postgres, outbound email, and HTTPS.

alternatives.name: UserJot
alternatives.desc: Two free boards, unlimited users, a public roadmap and a changelog. No user meter.

facts.install: Hosted signup with an email. No card.
facts.dataFormat: Feedback, votes, comments, roadmap and changelog entries live in UserJot's cloud. Internal format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: UserJot is a public board and changelog. It is not a private typed inbox, and the free plan stops at two boards.
facts.setupBlocker: Signup is clean. The free plan is two boards and drops custom domain, private boards, and guest posting to paid tiers.

alternatives.name: Sleekplan Indie
alternatives.desc: Unlimited feedback, a roadmap and a changelog for one admin. Branding is the rent.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then embed the widget or publish the hosted portal
facts.dataFormat: Feedback, votes, comments, roadmap items, changelog posts and widget config live in Sleekplan's cloud. Internal format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Indie is one administrator with visible branding. It is a public board, not a private typed inbox.
facts.setupBlocker: No install hurdle. The free plan is one admin, keeps Sleekplan branding, and locks custom domain and workflow controls behind paid plans.

alternatives.name: ClearFlask
alternatives.desc: Feedback, duplicates and a real roadmap. The Compose file is the least lightweight part.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with the project's bundled dependencies
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted records live in a DynamoDB-compatible store, indexes in MySQL/MariaDB or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, uploads in S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: ClearFlask covers the public feedback loop, but the AWS-shaped stack is heavier than TellTide's widget-and-inbox job.
facts.setupBlocker: Compose starts a large dependency stack. A public deploy still needs env, domain, TLS, email, and backups.

alternatives.name: Quackback
alternatives.desc: Posts, votes, duplicates, roadmap and changelog in one Compose file. Young, pin the image.

facts.dataFormat: Posts, votes, comments, users, roadmap items and changelog entries live in PostgreSQL.
facts.gapVsPaid: Quackback is a public Canny-style board you operate yourself, not a private typed inbox with a one-script widget.
facts.setupBlocker: You supply secrets, run Compose, put it behind HTTPS, configure email, and back up the database.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Canny Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: 25 tracked users and 5 managers. That is a cap, not a long-term replacement.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GitHub Issues
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A public engineering tracker. No customer widget, no private inbox, no product roadmap for people who do not live on GitHub.

notes: Private inbox first, public board second. Price checked on the homepage 2026-08-22.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for TellTide in an empty folder.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, and SQLite via better-sqlite3. Do not offer another stack.
The core loop is: embed a feedback widget on a site, store reviews, bugs, feature requests, and general comments in a private inbox, then publish selected feature requests to a public roadmap with votes and comments.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all data in a local SQLite file and make JSON/CSV export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Include a public widget script that opens a panel with four types: review (1-5 stars), general feedback, bug report, and feature request.
Optional name and email fields plus a message. Bugs get steps to reproduce. Feature requests get a short title.
An admin inbox at /inbox with filters for type and status (open, in progress, resolved, closed, declined).
Status updates, search, and a detail view.
A public roadmap at /roadmap that only shows items you explicitly publish, with votes and comments.
A simple widget designer: colors, launcher label, panel title, and position. Persist it and load it from the widget.
One documented snippet using a script tag with data-app-id="local".
README with setup, the SQLite file location, and how to embed the widget on a local HTML page.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Slack and email integrations, SSO, multi-tenant billing, and a changelog.
Deliberately leave out AI duplicate merging and revenue-weighted voting.
Finish by listing the exact commands to run it and where the SQLite file lives.
